significance: The royal temple within the Royal Palace compound at Phnom Penh, completed in the 19th century under King Norodom and later remodelled under Norodom Sihanouk with 5,329 silver floor tiles and Italian marble. It holds a small green crystal Buddha and a life-size gold Maitreya of 90 kg set with 9,584 diamonds, made in the palace workshops in 1906-07; Sihanouk was ordained there on 31 July 1947, and the Maitreya lost most of its diamonds during the civil war before restorations from 1985.
story: The Reamker, the Khmer telling of the Ramayana, runs in murals along 642 m of the enclosing wall, and the legend of Preah Ko Preah Keo is represented by two statues.
